title: Light constraints leave a scale to determine
question: What map can respect both light directions?
recap: Linearity and the two light directions constrain space and time to mix. Reciprocity and spatial symmetry then fix a remaining scale, with the positive choice connected to the identity.
premises: Use aligned inertial axes and coincident origins at zero time.
Assume homogeneous space and time so the coordinate map is linear.
Use the postulates together with reciprocity, spatial isotropy, and continuity at zero speed.
limitations: Preserving a light ray alone does not uniquely fix all transformation coefficients.
A spacetime interval or matrix is a later verification aid, not an unannounced 1905 premise.

overview.text: Linearity and the two light directions constrain space and time to mix. Reciprocity and spatial symmetry then fix a remaining scale, with the positive choice connected to the identity.

full.text: The moving origin follows \(x = vt\), so write \(x' = a(v)(x - vt)\). Requiring \(x' = ct'\) on \(x = ct\) and \(x' = -ct'\) on \(x = -ct\) fixes the time combination: \(t' = a(v)(t - vx/c^2)\). An overall scale \(a(v)\) remains.

full.spoken: The light constraints give a common coefficient multiplying x minus vt and t minus vx over c squared.

full.text: Applying the inverse with speed \(-v\) gives \(a(v)\,a(-v)\,(1 - v^2/c^2) = 1\). Isotropy identifies \(a(v)\) with \(a(-v)\). Continuity from \(a(0) = 1\) selects the positive square root.

full.spoken: The Lorentz factor is one over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared, giving the standard space and time transformation.

full.returnCaption: Return to what map can respect both light directions.

items: Use the moving origin to determine the combination x − vt.
Substitute both right-moving and left-moving light paths into the linear time map.
Solve the resulting coefficient constraints without setting the scale by hand.
Use isotropy to equate the positive-speed and negative-speed scales.
Choose the identity-connected positive solution, requiring |v| less than c.

margin.text: This compact two-light-direction derivation is an editorial reconstruction, not the source’s word-for-word synchronization derivation. Einstein’s printed \(\beta\) is the modern \(\gamma\) used here; his moving-system time \(\tau\) is not automatically proper time.
